stem:
Mona scores $18$ marks out of $20$ on one test and $22$ marks out of $25$ on another.

Which claim about comparing her percentages is correct?

options.text: $22$ is larger than $18$, so the second score is the higher percent even without comparing the different wholes.
Fair comparison is what produces the different wholes, so she skips making the bases comparable.
Convert both to percentages first ($90\%$ and $88\%$), because the wholes $20$ and $25$ differ.
Compare the raw scores on a third unrelated whole of $100$ marks she did not take.

teacher.key_rationale: Percentages with different wholes are not compared by raw marks alone. $18/20=90\%$ and $22/25=88\%$. Ignoring bases, reversing comparison into the wholes, or inventing a third whole all skip comparable bases.
